# About this book {.unnumbered}

Imagine watching a live lecture. You want the lecturer’s voice to arrive on time, the picture to stay close to live, and the system to work just as well when a hundred more people join. How do we make that happen?

**MoQ for the Curious** explains Media over QUIC from the first idea to a working mental model. We introduce each problem before the mechanism that solves it. You do not need to know QUIC, video compression, or the language of protocol specifications to begin.

[Start reading: What, Why and How →](docs/01-what-why-and-how/index.qmd)

## Where to begin

The first chapter explains what MoQ is and [how it compares with WebRTC](docs/01-what-why-and-how/index.qmd#how-does-moq-compare-with-webrtc). From there, we follow a live publication through its connection, tracks, subscriptions, relays, and player. The later chapters cover a first experiment, security, and debugging.

A fictional lecture runs through the examples. When a new term appears, we explain what it means and why it matters. The [glossary](docs/12-glossary/index.qmd) is here whenever a word gets in the way.

## A protocol still taking shape

This edition uses **MOQT draft-21**, published September 8, 2026, as its IETF baseline. It distinguishes that transport specification from the **moq.dev** implementation, **moq-lite**, and the **hang** media format. Draft-specific details and implementation examples are labeled throughout.

The research date is **September 16, 2026**. Each chapter links to primary sources; the [references](docs/13-references/index.qmd) explain the source policy and limitations. Example latency values are teaching aids, not benchmarks, and the upstream walkthrough commands have not been executed for this guide.

## About the approach

The approachable, concepts-first prose is inspired by [WebRTC for the Curious](https://webrtcforthecurious.com/docs/01-what-why-and-how/). The explanations, examples, and diagrams are original. The familiar online textbook presentation is inspired by [RLHF Book](https://rlhfbook.com/), and this site is built using Quarto’s standard book framework.

This is an independent guide. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the IETF, moq.dev, WebRTC for the Curious, or RLHF Book.
